reading_interface_boundary: The fixed SDK/public WHP getter accepts WHV_REGISTER_NAME and exposes no DebugCtl/LBR/LER/PT names. No documented direct host history getter was identified; TLFS identifiers remain a distinct namespace.

Guest architectural LBR use can employ model-supported control/read MSRs when virtualized support is exposed. The absence of a public WHP getter does not prove guest MSRs are the only possible interface across Windows: privileged TLFS and managed Hyper-V are different interfaces with distinct requirements.

Microsoft managed Hyper-V documentation exposes performance-monitoring hardware with Set-VMProcessor -Perfmon while VM is stopped. This is guest feature configuration, not a WHP partition-handle history getter. Host inventory reports neither Hyper-V module nor that cmdlet available; no configuration command was attempted.

Even working guest MSR access would be an instrumented capability experiment: additional guest instructions and VM transitions may affect the history. It cannot be labeled an untouched original-game predecessor without a preservation/ownership/loss contract.
